payload.title: How to Get Married in Brazil as a Foreigner
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often Australian and often with parents contributing, who picture a Brazilian beach or colonial-town wedding and want to know before they commit to a region whether foreigners can marry legally in Brazil, which documents to prepare and in what order (apostille, sworn translation and, for Australians, a Certificate of No Impediment), how the Cartório de Registro Civil process runs from habilitação to certidão de casamento, whether the certificate will be recognised at home, and whether Rio de Janeiro, Bahia and Trancoso, Fernando de Noronha, Florianópolis and Santa Catarina or Paraty suits the wedding they imagine.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation (speak with a Wedded Advisor) at /wonderland-concierge.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'getting married in brazil' are split between consular and expat pages written in legal shorthand and beach-wedding pages that skim the paperwork. This guide is written for any foreign couple, with the Australian side clearly marked, and in the order they act: can foreigners marry legally in Brazil; documents first (apostille, sworn translation into Portuguese, Certificate of No Impediment for Australians) and only then entry; the Cartório de Registro Civil steps (habilitação application, proclamas notice period, ceremony by a juiz de paz, certidão de casamento) explained in plain English with the Portuguese terms kept; getting the certificate ready for Australia (Apostille, recognition); what a beach or outdoor ceremony involves legally versus symbolically; seasons by region without a best month; and a business-free region chooser. Figure-free, dated once as at November 2026, sixth in the 'Getting Married in {Country}' series, with a link across to Brazilian wedding traditions.
outline_spine: Intro: direct answer in the first 100 words (foreign couples can marry legally in Brazil through a civil process at a Cartório de Registro Civil, as officially stated; this guide takes it step by step), then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways.
Can foreigners marry legally in Brazil? Civil marriage at the cartório and its legal effect, only as official sources state; 'as at November 2026' once.

Documents first, then entry: what the cartório asks foreign couples for (passport, birth certificate, proof of single status, apostille on foreign documents, sworn translation by a tradutor juramentado), the Australian Certificate of No Impediment (marked 'For Australians'), then entry to Brazil per official Brazilian and Smartraveller pages; no amounts, no processing times.

Step by step at the Cartório de Registro Civil: habilitação application, proclamas (notice) and any waiting period only as sourced, witnesses only as sourced, ceremony by a juiz de paz, signing, the certidão de casamento; 'a fee applies' only where a source says so.

Getting your certificate ready for Australia (marked 'For Australians'): Apostille on the Brazilian certificate, translation for Australian use and recognition at home only as Smartraveller or AGD state.

Beach and outdoor ceremonies: whether the legal ceremony can take place outside the cartório only as sourced; the option of a legal civil ceremony plus a symbolic celebration; questions to put to a venue (sole use, privacy, weather backup, deposits and contracts, step-free access).
When to marry: seasons and rainfall by region from official meteorological sources (INMET) labelled by location; no best month.

Choose your region: Rio de Janeiro, Bahia and Trancoso, Fernando de Noronha, Florianópolis and Santa Catarina, Paraty; one or two lines each from official tourism sources (Embratur / Visit Brasil); no businesses, no ranking; /expert-advice/brazilian-wedding-traditions once.
Venues and planning: one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts.md (primary CTA); /magazine once; never legal paperwork help.
Close: plan your Brazil wedding with a Wedded Advisor (closing CTA).
